lessons.description: Add try/except handling to a colour-processing function and test it against supplied sensor-blackout samples. Handle ZeroDivisionError and return a safe fallback so unexpected input does not crash the program.
lessons.template:
import time
from lineRobot import Robot
robot = Robot()

def detect_color_name(r, g, b):
    total = r + g + b

    # TODO: Protect the math below with try-except ZeroDivisionError
    # If an error occurs, print a warning and return "Unknown"

    r_ratio = r / total
    g_ratio = g / total

    if r_ratio > 0.4:
        return "Red"
    elif g_ratio > 0.4:
        return "Green"
    else:

lessons.name: Code Clinic (Refactoring)
lessons.description: Refactor a working line-following and colour-detection script into clear functions, named constants and a simple main loop. Improve program structure and readability while preserving behaviour and the sensor-error safety net.
lessons.template:
import time
from lineRobot import Robot
from octoliner import Octoliner
from tcs3472 import tcs3472
import machine

r = Robot()
b = machine.I2C(scl=machine.Pin(22), sda=machine.Pin(21), freq=100000)
o = Octoliner()
o.begin(b)
o.set_sensitivity(240)
t = tcs3472(b)

v = 20
k = 15
last = "Floor"
line = 500

print("Starting Spaghetti Mission")

while True:
    # Sensor 1 logic
    sa = o.analog_read_all()
    print(sa)
    if max(sa) < line:
        r.stop()
        break
    
    # Navigation
    p = o.track_line()
    res = k * p
    
    # Sensor 2 logic
    cr, cg, cb = t.rgb()
    tot = cr + cg + cb
    
    # Dangerous math!
    rr = cr / tot
    gr = cg / tot
    br = cb / tot
    
    c = "Floor"
    if rr > 0.5:
        c = "Red"
    elif gr > 0.4:
        c = "Green"
    elif br > 0.4:
        c = "Blue"
    
    if c != last and c != "Floor":
        print("Found mineral:", c)
        last = c

    # Output to motors
    m1 = int(v + res)
    m2 = int(v - res)
    r.run_motors_speed(m1, m2)
    
    time.sleep(0.05)
